question: What is the main finding in the urine of someone with nephrotic syndrome?
explanation: Damage to the filtering membrane of the kidney allows large amounts of blood proteins to leak into the urine. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why does widespread swelling happen in patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: Blocked lymph vessels stop normal skin drainage
options.B: High salt intake overworks the kidney tubes
options.C: High heart output pushes blood into the legs
options.D: Low blood protein levels pull fluid out of vessels into tissues

explanation: Losing blood proteins lowers the pressure that keeps fluid inside blood vessels, causing it to leak into surrounding tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the most frequent cause of nephrotic syndrome in young children?
explanation: Minimal change disease is responsible for the vast majority of primary nephrotic syndrome cases in children. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h2)

question: When a diabetic patient develops nephrotic syndrome, how is this type classified?

options.A: A birth defect present since early pregnancy
options.B: Kidney failure caused entirely by heavy metal poisoning
options.C: An infection limited strictly to the renal pelvis
options.D: Kidney damage triggered by a whole-body disease

explanation: Secondary nephrotic syndrome happens when a systemic illness, like diabetes, damages the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which blood test result usually drops low in a patient with nephrotic syndrome?
explanation: Constantly losing protein through the urine causes a significant drop in circulating blood albumin levels. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient presents with puffy eyes and foamy urine. Which test confirms the main problem?

options.A: Random blood glucose test for diabetes
options.D: Complete blood count to check for infection

explanation: Measuring protein released over 24 hours directly shows the amount of leakage coming from the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the standard first-line medication used to treat minimal change disease?
explanation: Corticosteroids like prednisone are the main treatment to calm the immune response causing the kidney leak. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why are ACE inhibitors prescribed for patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: To reduce pressure inside the kidney filters and lower protein loss
options.B: To lower blood cholesterol and fat levels
options.C: To prevent deep vein blood clots
options.D: To stimulate bone marrow to make red blood cells

explanation: ACE inhibitors relax the kidney blood vessels, reducing pressure inside the filters to slow down protein loss. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which diet change is most important for managing swelling in nephrotic syndrome?
explanation: Limiting salt intake prevents the body from holding onto extra water and making the swelling worse. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is a very high protein diet discouraged for chronic protein loss in the kidneys?

options.A: It causes dangerous jumps in blood potassium
options.C: It forces remaining kidney filters to work harder and worsens scarring
options.D: It stops the liver from making cholesterol

explanation: Eating too much protein makes the working nephrons strain harder, increasing filtration pressure and speeding up kidney damage. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h5)

question: Losing which protective substance puts nephrotic patients at high risk for infection?
explanation: Losing immunoglobulins in the urine strips the body of the antibodies it needs to fight off common bacterial germs. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is an important nursing action for a hospitalized patient with generalized swelling?

options.A: Applying warm compresses to puffy eyelids
options.B: Checking daily weights at the same time every day
options.C: Massaging swollen legs to move trapped fluid
options.D: Encouraging high fluid intake to flush the kidneys

explanation: Weighing the patient daily gives the most accurate, objective measure of fluid gain or loss during treatment. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h6)

question: What early sign of a returning condition should patients watch for at home?

options.C: Sudden weight gain and facial puffiness

explanation: Water building back up from protein loss quickly shows up as facial swelling and sudden weight gain. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)

question: What instruction is critical for a patient taking long-term steroids?

options.A: Double the dose if your joints feel stiff
options.B: Take the medication only on an empty stomach
options.C: Stop the drug right away if you gain a little weight
options.D: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without a doctor's advice

explanation: Stopping steroids abruptly can cause serious adrenal gland problems and bring back the kidney disease. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)
